data.exact_reserve_text: During 2019, gross ultimate claims in respect of prior underwriting years (2017 and prior) increased by $64.2m ($29.5m net of RI). Of this, $58.3m ($26.9m net of RI) relates to Casualty division losses on 2016 and prior underwriting years of account. The remainder is driven by newly occurring large losses, mostly from multi-year construction policies in the Tech division.
data.standardized_narrative: During 2019, Syndicate 1919 experienced a gross prior year reserve strengthening of $64.2 million, representing 9.08% of its opening gross claims outstanding. This adverse development was primarily driven by large loss development and adverse claims development on older underwriting years. Specifically, $58.3 million of the strengthening related to Casualty division losses on 2016 and prior underwriting years, while the remaining $5.9 million was due to newly occurring large losses from multi-year construction policies in the Technical Risks (Property) division.

data.data_quality_notes: The explicit prior year development figure of $64.2m from narrative text on page 42 is used, as it is a direct statement of ultimate claims increase for prior years. This figure differs from a calculation based on the gross claims development triangle on page 41, which would yield approximately $92.577m. The narrative figure is prioritized as it directly addresses 'gross ultimate claims in respect of prior underwriting years'. No specific named events were identified as causes for the prior year development, only general 'large loss development' and 'adverse claims development'. The 'RDS event' table on page 38 lists hypothetical scenarios for the 2020 forecast, not actual events impacting 2019 results.
